answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with stake-bonded reputation: every identity must lock a refundable bond and earn trust only through attested work over time, like a lotus that grows slowly from the mud rather than appearing overnight. A single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents faces a gale of costs, because each identity needs its own locked capital, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Honest agents keep their oasis of accumulated reputation and rewards, while attackers pay full price for every fake face and lose it the moment they cheat.
